content:
Most of us understand when an obvious or game breaking bug needs to be fixed and would not complain about those. (e.g. the Pontos Pickman interaction was rightly patched shortly after release)

However, there have been many more niche interactions that have been changed, resulting in either a removal of a quality of life or reduction in power level of a unit/wheel a long time after their release. (e.g. Pontos, Miryam, Lily and now Corposant)

When something has settled in the meta, players have formed their expectations about certain play patterns or performance; To change this without any prior communication and compensation can make a player feel cheated, I certainly feel that way myself. Furthermore, this seems to be carried out more and more often by the dev as a matter of course, with no consideration to players that have invested monetarily or emotionally into these units.

To sum up, outside of game breaking or balance shifting bugs, changes that will result in nerfs to a unit or wheel should either be avoided if possible, or at least communicated much in advance and the player base compensated adequately when implemented.

content:
At first when I played with Caraboo, I thought that her "Missed Chance" delay was quite funny in a sense (at least on stream) and was part of her capriciousness. Well, after doing H5-11 Cocoon with a relatively weak team, needless to say I'm not laughing any more. <:Helot_slack_off:1459092159465521184> 

I personally think Caraboo is a powerful character overall (some might disagree), but the Missed Chance effect is extremely damaging even compared to the other particularly bad negative prices like "Veiled Malice" Fragile. Caraboo's Missed Chance (and to a degree her in general) would fit very well in a roguelike deckbuilder game with a slower turn-by-turn pace, which was also mostly balanced around being a funny type of game where the aim is to create really overpowered synergies with the help of RNG or fail.

When you think about it, Morimens is just not that kind of game. Yes a lot of things in the game are RNG, but no other single RNG instance is nearly as punitive as Missed Chance can be. Getting a Missed Chance effect in the crucial last one or two turns of a tough fight is **practically speaking the same as getting no effect**.  If you get several of these in a row, it can single-handedly lose you a fight you would've won if it gave you Gilded Words/Veiled Malice... this is not a hypothetical, this did happen to me and I had to redo the whole 13 turn bossfight. <:Saya_caught:1513123193341349968> No other character before now has the potential to lose you the fight solo by a chain of poor luck like this.

I genuinely think that Missed Chance effects at critical times are the biggest reason a lot of people don't like playing her. I think that it was a cute idea on paper, but Morimens can be a pretty tough game and you need to have more control over your cards played. Bricking hard on one turn often has the potential to kill you instantly.

(Alternative ideas here https://discord.com/channels/1131791637933199470/1542907680522510418/1542910534171754608)
thread_title: Caraboo Blessing "Missed Chance" should be reworked

content:
Potential alternatives I came up with - these are just suggestions, I'm not saying they're pristine ideas

**1) When you trigger "Missed Chance", you are given the option to bribe Caraboo with 7 Black Sigil. If you pay the fee, the effect works immediately. Otherwise it is delayed for 2 turns.**

*I think 7 Sigil is a significant enough price to hurt, but you can control it by saving some for bossfights.*

**2) When you trigger "Missed Chance", the effect works immediately as would be normal, but then the *next* Blessing you use both pays its own Price and also is delayed for 2 turns.**

*This is a strong negative effect which is very similar to the current, but the difference is you can control this one by sacrificing other Blessings. The logic of this is put simply so that if you need a Posse to win and you have 2 Keyflare Blessings in hand, you will definitely be able to trigger at least one of them no matter what, as opposed to missing both of them with the current system and just dying.*

**3) "Missed Chance" effect is replaced with "Blood Tithe"**

Blood Tithe triggers the effect as normal, but at the start of the next turn a negative effect is triggered based on the Blessing from last turn.
+STR: -STR of half the STR gained.
STR down: Enemy gains 50% Temporary STR of the amount lost last turn.
Draw 8: Discard 3 cards of your choice from your hand (pretty crippling ngl)
+6 Arithmetica: Lose 2 Arithmetica (shouldn't be half because losing Arith at start of turn is awful let's be honest)
+2000 Keyflare: Lose 1000 Keyflare
+200% Temporary DMG Amp: -100% Temporary DMG Amp
25 Team Aliemus: Everyone loses 13 Aliemus.

*This might be too similar to Gilded Words really, but I just wanted to put an alternate example suggestion which I feel would be a very powerful downside, but more balanced and able to be played around.*

Dear Support Team,

I'm writing to report persistent crashing issues on my iPad (9th generation, running the latest iPadOS). The crashes happen regularly, but they are most severe during the traphase mode.

What happens:

· When entering a traphase battle, the game either freezes completely or crashes to the home screen.
· Sometimes the crash occurs in the middle of a traphase fight.
· In some cases, the game crashes twice during a single traphase session.
· Outside of traphase, the game may also freeze or crash after about 20–30 minutes of normal play.

 I've already set all graphics settings to the minimum, but this did not improve the situation at all.
 I've also restarted the device and made sure no other apps are running in the background.

This issue makes traphase almost unplayable, and it's very frustrating. Please let me know if you need any additional details.

I would appreciate any advice or fix you can offer. Thank you for your time!🙇‍♀️

content:
In the recent update of 2.6 there has been a change to Corposants Pilots and their interaction with Horla wheel. While labelled as a Bugfix this ends up being a straight up nerf to Corpo as a character and her viability. Now why is this an issue and why do i think its been incredibly poorly handled?

1. Consistency: 
The interaction between Corposant and Horlas Wheel has been working for over a year already, players have correctly identified that its by far her best wheel based on the assumptions the game works as intended by the developers. If people are right to assume interactions between characters and wheels have been in place for over a year then it should be safe to assume developers wont just nerf them overnight.

2. Timing:
It strikes me as odd that both Corpo and Last Verse have been on rerun banners and many players got essentially tricked into investing, into both of these things by their incredible synergy. In my case for example i invested in both +12 character and +12 wheel, which while a luxury investment, now feels incredibly lackluster and the developers rerunning both without a disclaimer is almost malicious intent. Another thing that i will add on to this point is that the Dtide changes are around the corner and...

3. The META:
Corposant is not overpowered? She is a good unit for sure and her interactions with horla wheel are amazing but? This was not problematic. Nobody was abusing this interaction to break content or ruining encounters. With the game mode changes around the corner this feels like a loss of 20% of Corpos power while shes not even one of the most likely Meta units for Nightmare/Madness clears

I would kindly and respectfully ask for these changes to be seriously thought over. Either in a way thats just adjusting numbers for the power lost (20-25% buff) or creating a unique interaction where pilots are treated as a secondary command card created by Corposant, giving them the same benefit as Aurita Gland Division of not being affected by Arithmetica Harmony. Otherwise this feels like a slap in the face to every Corposant player who was excited to play her after her very very recent rerun, thank you.

content:
With how recent divine realm units have been absolutely powercreeping the ass out of older characters, it feels like it would've been more reasonable to reclassify Corpo and Miryam's buff cards as derived cards so they could still at least perform at the lvl they've been performing at for the past year. The nerf is so arbitrary. 

Lily's went under the radar despite being a 50% nerf because using her as a poison dps wasn't really viable anyways, and the 24 fiasco overshadowed her. It was still infuriating since poison teams are already behind in terms of the meta! There was no harm in leaving it be! All it did was make the unit people had already invested in (albeit for different uses) worse!

Corposant is central to an entire playstyle. She is *essential* to Discard. There is no unit that substitutes what she offers, and a 20% cut to her viability sucks. Is this just meant to steer us towards investing in her wheel? Because that's still not gonna happen. Horla's wheel is still good! At AA Corpo's a crazy unit, but that goes for a lot of AA units! You've stated yourselves that AA wouldn't be factors to the game's balance (debatable, but that's neither here nor there). She's functioned like this for a whole year. There wasn't even a hint this was "a bug we're working on fixing". You can hardly play dumb to a *whole year* of your entire community habitually using this wheel with Corpo and writing *multiple guides in multiple languages* referencing this interaction. Why is it *now* a year later that it's being addressed like a footnote?

Every single time. Nerfs are put through again and again under the justification of "bug fixes" despite being long-accepted interactions, all so you can maintain the stance of "Uwu we don't nerf, we only buff!!" and every single time it only damages your players' trust in your competency as game devs.

It's like every other patch you're compelled to push through something stupid, all while ignoring things that could improve.
